key_insight: Dense, low-porosity Fe-based amorphous coatings improve long-term corrosion resistance, while increasing humidity reduces friction and wear.
engineering_relevance: Controlling detonation-spray parameters to minimize coating defects could improve the durability of coated Q235 carbon steel.
method: Deposit Fe-based amorphous coatings on Q235 steel using varied detonation-spray parameters.
Assess droplet morphology, coating microstructure, and long-term corrosion behavior.
Evaluate friction and wear under different humidity conditions using Si3N4 balls.
evidence_signal: The abstract links greater porosity to poorer long-term corrosion resistance and reports decreasing friction coefficients and wear rates as humidity increases.
watch_item: The abstract provides no numerical performance values or humidity ranges, limiting application-specific durability estimates.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
